title: Kikwiflow deploy-grade process definition
description: Structural companion to skills/model-kikwi-process — matches ProcessDefinitionDeployRequest/FlowNodeDefinition/SequenceFlowDefinition. Every field/requirement here is checked against two things: kikwi-model's plain Java records (nothing is 'required' at the model level by itself) and kikwi-core's DeployValidator (the only thing that actually rejects a deploy). Tier A below means DeployValidator actually enforces it today (a real required/enum/conditional constraint here); tier B means it's documented/expected behavior the engine does NOT check at deploy time — described in prose only, on the field itself, and never turned into a schema constraint, so this schema never rejects a process the real engine would accept. If the engine evolves, re-verify field lists/tiers against those two source locations (or an equivalent generated ground-truth schema) before trusting this file over them.
$comment: Draft 2020-12 (not 07) is required here: per-node-type schemas below combine a shared baseNodeFields definition via allOf with unevaluatedProperties:false, which is the only way to reject a field that's valid on one node type but not another (e.g. catch executor set on a JOIN_GATEWAY) without duplicating every type's full field list. Deliberately excluded (no field for these anywhere below): transitionType on sequence flows (appears in the document-java-as-kikwi skill's own edge shape, and in some prose docs, but SequenceFlowDefinition has no such field) — see kikwi-docs.schema.json for the sibling schema that does include it, and skills/model-kikwi-process/SKILL.md Step 2 for why the two intentionally diverge here.

key.description: kebab-case business key — what KikwiflowEngine.startProcess().byKey(...) targets. Redeploying under the same key versions over (running instances stay on their original version).

sla.description: Accepted by the parser but not read anywhere in kikwi-core today — vestigial.

defaultStartPoint.description: Should be a key present in flowNodes, identifying a DEFAULT_START_EVENT node. Tier B: NOT validated at deploy time — only resolved the first time a process instance is started, and fails then if it doesn't resolve.

flowNodes.description: Keyed by node id. By convention the map key should equal the node's own "id" field, but that consistency is tier B — never checked by the engine.

extensionProperties.description: Free-form string-to-string bag, opaque to the engine core. Two reserved keys are used by convention (the Kikwiflow visual modeler): 'kikwi:documentation' (Markdown, may include ```mermaid fenced blocks) and 'kikwi:documentationLink' (a URL or a project-relative path, the latter only resolving inside the VS Code extension) — by UI convention the two are mutually exclusive, but neither the engine nor this schema enforces that. Present at process, node, and sequence-flow level.

layoutCoordinates.description: Diagram positioning only — no effect on execution.

sequenceFlow.description: Lives inside a node's own "outgoing" array — there's no separate top-level sequence-flow collection.

expectedAnswer.description: Only meaningful on EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY outgoing edges — compared by plain string equality against whatever the gateway's AnswerProvider resolves to. No expression/condition language exists.

targetNodeId.description: Should be a key present in flowNodes. Tier B: an unresolved id only fails the first time this edge is actually taken, at runtime.

isDefault.description: Taken when the resolved answer is non-null and no expectedAnswer matched. At most one true per EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY — enforced separately on that gateway's outgoing array, tier A (see exclusiveGateway below).

handlesNull.description: Taken when the gateway's AnswerProvider resolves to null — checked ahead of expectedAnswer/isDefault matching.

positionHandlers.description: Intermediate waypoints for diagram rendering only — no effect on execution.

extensionProperties.description: A real, persisted field on SequenceFlowDefinition — do not assume edges can't carry kikwi:documentation/kikwi:documentationLink or other metadata; they can, exactly like nodes.

labelPosition.description: Only set when a human manually drags the edge's label chip in the visual modeler (mainly relevant on EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY edges). Absent/null means the UI recalculates the label position automatically — don't synthesize a default {x,y} here; round-trip exactly what was saved.

sourceHandle.description: Opaque id of the source node's outgoing visual handle in the modeler's graph (e.g. "right", "right-2" when a node has more than one visual output on the same side). No closed vocabulary — UI-defined, passed through as plain text.

id.description: Should equal this node's own key in flowNodes — the engine resolves cross-references (targetNodeId, attachedToRef, boundaryEventIds, ...) against the map key, not this field. A mismatch is tier B, never checked.

commitBefore.description: When true, the engine persists state and returns control immediately instead of continuing synchronously — a background worker later polls for the pending work. Not BPMN asyncBefore; there's no message bus.

outgoing.description: null when omitted from the JSON — an omitted "outgoing" and an explicit "outgoing": null are the same at runtime, NOT [].

retryPolicy.description: Only used by EXECUTABLE_TASK.retryPolicy. When null entirely, the engine falls back to an app-level default-retry-interval config instead of any of these fields.

initialInterval.description: ISO-8601 duration (e.g. "PT10S"). Tier B: semantically the base interval for EXPONENTIAL_BACKOFF, but not required at deploy time — omitted/null falls back to a hardcoded default at runtime, it does not fail deploy.

multiplier.description: EXPONENTIAL_BACKOFF only. Defaults to 2.0 at runtime when null.

maxInterval.description: ISO-8601 duration cap on the computed interval. EXPONENTIAL_BACKOFF only.

intervals.description: LINEAR only — ISO-8601 durations indexed by attempt number, clamped to the last entry once exhausted. Tier B: not required at deploy time — falls back to a hardcoded PT1M if empty/null, does not fail deploy.

type.description: KNOWN ENGINE GAP: CRON is not actually parsed as a real cron expression today — it falls through to the exact same Duration.parse(expression) path as RATE_DURATION. Don't author a real cron string expecting cron semantics yet.

expression.description: ISO-8601 duration (e.g. "PT1H") — used for RATE_DURATION and, today, also for CRON (see above). Tier B: not required at deploy time regardless of type.

fixedDates.description: FIXED_DATES only — ISO-8601 instants; the evaluator picks the first future date. Tier B: not required at deploy time.

maxOccurrences.description: 1-based cap on recurrence cycles — with maxOccurrences=3 the timer fires on cycles 1, 2, 3 and never schedules a 4th. null means unbounded recurrence.

value.description: Literal text when type=LITERAL, or the name of a process variable to interpolate when type=VARIABLE.

correlationTemplate.description: One entry expected per key when the owning node's catchType=GROUP; a single entry for STANDALONE.

correlationKeySourceBase.description: Shared correlation-key resolution contract, implemented by EVENT_CATCHER, BOUNDARY_INTERRUPTIVE_CATCH_EVENT and EVENT_THROWER. All four providerType-conditional requirements below are tier A — enforced at deploy time identically for all three node types.

providerBean.description: CorrelationKeysProvider Spring bean name — required non-blank and resolved at deploy time when providerType=BEAN.

providerVariable.description: Process variable name — required non-blank at deploy time when providerType=VARIABLE.

staticKey.description: Literal correlation key (not staticValue — that name is reserved for timer due-dates) — required non-blank at deploy time when providerType=STATIC.

correlationTemplates.description: Required non-empty at deploy time when providerType=TEMPLATE.

flowNodeUnion.description: One entry of the flowNodes map. Dispatched on "type" — each branch routes to the matching $defs/nodeTypes/* schema, which independently closes itself against fields that don't belong to that specific node type.

endEvent.description: outgoing being empty is tier B (not enforced at deploy) — see reference/validation-checklist.md.

executableTask.description: Runs a Java TaskHandler synchronously on the acquiring thread.

executor.description: Spring TaskHandler bean name. Tier A, but only IF non-blank — a blank/omitted executor deploys fine and only fails the first time this node is actually reached.

boundaryEventIds.description: Tier A allowlist (the referenced ids' own types aren't checkable by this schema — cross-node reference): only BOUNDARY_NON_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER or BOUNDARY_ERROR_HANDLER — no interruptive timer/catch event, since this task has no safe interruption point mid-execution.

externalTask.description: A wait state, completed from outside the engine.

boundaryEventIds.description: Tier B: no dedicated deploy-time allowlist branch exists for this host type — each boundary event enforces its own attachedToRef-target rule instead (e.g. BOUNDARY_INTERRUPTIVE_CATCH_EVENT independently requires EXTERNAL_TASK or TIMER_TASK).

exclusiveGateway.description: Routes to exactly one outgoing edge by string-matching an AnswerProvider's resolved answer against each edge's expectedAnswer.

defaultFlow.description: Informational only — the engine never reads this field at runtime; only outgoing[].isDefault decides the actual default edge.

providerBean.description: AnswerProvider Spring bean name — required non-blank and resolved at deploy time when providerType=BEAN.

providerVariable.description: Process variable name — required non-blank at deploy time when providerType=VARIABLE.

outgoing.description: Same shape as the common sequence flow, plus a gateway-specific tier-A constraint: at most one entry may set isDefault=true. Zero default edges is legal.

parallelGateway.description: Fans out to every outgoing edge unconditionally.

targetJoinId.description: Id of the JOIN_GATEWAY that closes this fork. Tier B: no deploy-time branch exists for PARALLEL_GATEWAY/JOIN_GATEWAY at all today — an unresolved or wrong-typed target only fails at runtime, and 0/1 outgoing edges deploy fine too, they just won't behave like a real fork.

joinGateway.description: Waits for every branch spawned by the matching PARALLEL_GATEWAY, then continues via its own outgoing[0].

sourceSplitId.description: Id of the originating PARALLEL_GATEWAY. Purely informational — never read at runtime.

boundaryInterruptiveTimer.description: A single-fire timer attached to a host node; firing interrupts the host.

attachedToRef.description: Id of the node this boundary timer is attached to.

providerType.description: Tier B: NOT enforced at deploy time — a missing/mismatched provider only fails at runtime, when the timer is due.

staticValue.description: ISO-8601 duration (e.g. "PT1H") or an absolute ISO-8601 instant — absolute-instant parsing is tried first, falling back to duration.

boundaryNonInterruptiveTimer.description: A recurring timer attached to a host node; firing does NOT interrupt the host.

boundaryErrorHandler.description: Synchronous try/catch semantics on the host's thrown errorCode. The only boundary event type allowed on an EXECUTABLE_TASK.

errorCode.description: null means a wildcard/catch-all handler. The engine picks the first boundary handler (in the host's boundaryEventIds list order) whose errorCode is null or equals the thrown code — no explicit most-specific-first ordering.

boundaryInterruptiveCatchEvent.description: Waits for a correlated event; firing interrupts the host.

attachedToRef.description: Tier A: must point to a node whose type is EXTERNAL_TASK or TIMER_TASK — no other host is accepted, not even EXECUTABLE_TASK or EVENT_CATCHER (this schema can't verify the referenced node's actual type — cross-node reference).

timerTask.description: A main-flow (not boundary) single-fire timer. Not a WaitState declared elsewhere, not Executable.

commitBefore.description: Whatever's declared here is overridden at runtime — a TIMER_TASK is always treated as commitBefore=true, since a timer can never execute synchronously.

providerType.description: Tier B: NOT enforced at deploy time — a missing/mismatched provider only fails at runtime, when the timer is due.

staticValue.description: ISO-8601 duration or absolute ISO-8601 instant — same parsing rule as BOUNDARY_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER.staticValue.

boundaryEventIds.description: Tier A allowlist: BOUNDARY_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER, BOUNDARY_NON_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER, or BOUNDARY_INTERRUPTIVE_CATCH_EVENT. No BOUNDARY_ERROR_HANDLER — a TIMER_TASK has no synchronous handler to try/catch.

eventCatcher.description: A wait state resolving one or more correlation keys and waiting for matching correlated events (STANDALONE = 1 key, GROUP = scatter-gather over N keys).

then.$comment: Tier A: STATIC always resolves exactly one key, which makes no sense combined with GROUP's scatter-gather semantics.

boundaryEventIds.description: Tier A allowlist: only BOUNDARY_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER or BOUNDARY_NON_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER node ids.

catchType.description: STANDALONE resolves exactly one key; GROUP is scatter-gather over N keys (matchPolicy decides ALL vs ANY).

eventThrower.description: A main-flow node (not a WaitState) that fires a correlated event and continues immediately. v1 policy is FAIL: if no catcher is currently waiting for the thrown key, the node fails and goes through the normal incident/retry path — never silently ignored.

callActivityCoordinator.description: Starts one or more independent child ProcessInstances (a subprocess call).

boundaryEventIds.description: Tier A allowlist: only BOUNDARY_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER or BOUNDARY_NON_INTERRUPTIVE_TIMER — no error handler, no catch event.

calledElement.description: Key of the process to call as a subprocess. Tier A: required non-blank. NOT validated that a process with this key actually exists/is deployed.

collectionVariable.description: Process variable expected to resolve to a List at runtime — one child ProcessInstance per element (or a single implicit null element if omitted). Not validatable at deploy time; the engine has no variable-type system.

elementVariable.description: Only valid together with collectionVariable — tier A: deploy-time error if set without it.

iterationMode.description: null is treated as PARALLEL at runtime. SEQUENTIAL starts only the first branch's child process and drips the rest as earlier children complete.
